clue.text: What the tabloids call Susan Boyle's badly trained assistant

parts.words: What the tabloids call Susan Boyle
parts.note: SuBo is the tabloid nickname for the singer Susan Boyle

indicators.note: badly says the letters of trained are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A tabloid jibe that the singer Susan Boyle's helper has had poor training.
explanation.walkthrough: SUBO, the British tabloids' nickname for the Britain's Got Talent singer, is followed by RDINATE, the letters of TRAINED rearranged as 'badly' says.
explanation.definitionFit: A subordinate is someone of lower rank who works under and helps another, much as an assistant does.

clue.text: P-plagiarise digital version

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft
to plagiarise is to copy someone else's work

explanation.surface: A stammered accusation of plagiarising a digital edition.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'P-' looks like a stutter, but it is a separate piece of wordplay: in music, p (piano) means play softly.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft copy is a document held electronically rather than printed on paper, as opposed to a hard copy.

clue.text: Whittle down first choice

parts.note: down means low in spirits, blue
to whittle wood is to chip away at it

explanation.surface: Pare something down to make your preferred pick.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces appear in the clue in the opposite order to the answer; 'Whittle down' reads as one phrase meaning reduce.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-chip company or player is a top-quality, reliable one, so a premier pick.

clue.text: Cool drink to quickly follow extra lessons

parts.note: a refresher is a cooling, reviving drink
to course is to chase game swiftly, as hounds do hares

explanation.surface: An instruction to down a cold drink and hurry after it.
explanation.walkthrough: Coursing is hunting in which dogs pursue hares by sight, so 'to course' is to follow at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher course is a short set of classes that updates or revives skills a person already has.

clue.text: Up for international title boxing the French

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the title wraps around what follows

parts.note: a title is a name

explanation.surface: Talk of an international boxing title involving the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' tempts as the sport in a title fight; here it means that NAME holds THE and FR.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the frame is to be under consideration, as a candidate is when up for a job or prize.

clue.text: Dangerous having no hospital open

indicators.note: having no says the hospital letter is lost from the word

parts.note: hairy is informal for dangerous or frightening

explanation.surface: A warning that it is risky when no hospital is open.
explanation.definitionFit: An airy room or space is spacious and well ventilated, uncluttered and unenclosed.

clue.text: Cricket ball teen smashed finds extra cover?

indicators.note: smashed means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teenager hits a cricket ball and finds a fielder at extra cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Extra cover is a cricket fielding position, which suits the surface; the question mark flags the pun on a bed's additional covering.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric blanket is a heated layer added to a bed, literally an additional covering.

clue.text: Secretaries knocked back juice

indicators.note: knocked back says the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: PAs are personal assistants, secretaries

explanation.surface: Office workers downing a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' suggests drinking, which suits the juice, but it signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sap is the fluid that circulates in a plant, its natural juice.

clue.text: Labour's got a new catchphrase

parts.note: labour is hard work, a slog; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: The Labour Party has adopted a fresh motto.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital L makes Labour look like the political party, but it is just hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a short memorable phrase, as used in advertising or politics.

clue.text: Mount Etna deposits somewhat academic

indicators.note: in a down clue, to mount is to go upwards, so the letters are read from the bottom up
somewhat says only part of the words is used, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: The volcano on Sicily leaves material of some scholarly interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like part of the name Mount Etna; it is the instruction to read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant is an overly academic person, fussy about formal rules and minor details of learning.

clue.text: Screw up and down

definitions.meaning: second meaning: soft fine fibres, like a bird's down

explanation.walkthrough: 'up and down' looks like a single phrase; it splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluff means both to botch an attempt and the light downy material that gathers on fabric.

clue.text: Considerably more than 25 taking hour in church

indicators.note: taking means holding inside, so the hour goes within

parts.note: 25 is the answer to clue 25 across, a golfer's support
the fold is a church congregation, the flock

explanation.surface: Something well beyond 25, with an hour spent at church.
explanation.walkthrough: The number 25 is not a quantity but a cross-reference to the answer of 25 across, TEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Threefold means tripled, so something increased threefold is substantially greater.

clue.text: Early riser to turn up regularly revealing beer belly

parts.note: to cock something, like a hat brim or ear, is to turn it upwards

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter is taken from the words

explanation.surface: Getting up early and showing off a paunch from drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel is a young rooster, famed for crowing at dawn, so it rises with the sun.

clue.text: Pull street artist in

parts.note: an RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Bring a street performer inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain or pull something is to drag or tug at it hard; also a pulled muscle.

clue.text: Filling in pool — oddly exciting without spades

indicators.note: oddly says the first and third letters of the word are taken
without says the spades letter is removed from the word

parts.note: something exciting is pulsating, throbbing with energy
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Filling a pool is thrilling, without needing spades to dig.
explanation.definitionFit: Populating a place means filling it with inhabitants or occupants.

clue.text: Choir plan working with him and orchestra?

indicators.note: working means operating in a new arrangement, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A choir's plan to work with a man and an orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the answer is usually the first part of an orchestra's name rather than a noun on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Philharmonic is the word in the names of many symphony orchestras, such as the London Philharmonic.

clue.text: Corroborate name in accordance with detective to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with says the first pieces come at the start, before the name

parts.note: under the rules means in accordance with them
a PI is a private investigator, a detective

explanation.surface: Backing up a name in line with what a detective first said.
explanation.definitionFit: To underpin a claim is to support or strengthen it, so to confirm it.

clue.text: Key to speak without a debate initially being guided

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard

indicators.note: without says the letter a is removed from the word

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A key point before speaking at a debate under guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' acts on 'a': ORATE loses its A to give ORTE, and 'debate initially' then adds D.
explanation.definitionFit: Escorted means accompanied and led along, so being guided by someone.

clue.text: Criminal mob dumps most of Eric 'n Ernie's output — for this?

indicators.note: criminal means corrupt or bent, so the letters are twisted into a new order
most of says the final letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: 'n is a shortened and, giving its letter N

explanation.surface: A crime gang dumping much of what comedians Eric and Ernie produced.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric 'n Ernie suggests Morecambe and Wise, the comedy double act, but ERNIE is the machine that picks winning Premium Bond numbers in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Premium Bonds are UK savings bonds entered into a monthly prize draw whose winning numbers are generated by a machine called ERNIE.

clue.text: Poem succeeded online?

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
online means on the net, the internet

explanation.surface: A poem that found success on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a fourteen-line verse form, a specific type of poem.

clue.text: Check steps — assuming foxtrot

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the foxtrot letter is taken inside

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps over a fence
Foxtrot is F in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Checking dance steps while doing a foxtrot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steps' and 'foxtrot' set up a dance floor; the steps are those of a stile over a field fence.
explanation.definitionFit: To stifle something is to suppress or restrain it, so to hold it in check.

clue.text: Group of seven stars making right personal trainer choice

indicators.note: making says one letter is turned into something else, a replacement

parts.note: Orion is a constellation whose shape is traced by seven bright stars
PT stands for physical training, here a personal trainer

explanation.surface: Star personal trainers, and a choice about the right one.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is one of the alternatives available, a possible choice.

clue.text: Jan, a pole dancing little hottie?

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jan pole-dancing is a small, attractive person.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hottie' is slang for an attractive person; the question mark flags a small hot chilli.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalapeño is a small, hot green chilli pepper, a punning sense of a hottie.

clue.text: In Washington DC — check legislation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in American English a restaurant check
second meaning: draft legislation put before a parliament or Congress

explanation.walkthrough: Washington DC hints at Congress passing laws, which suits the second meaning; the first is just American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is both the American check for a meal and a proposed law.

clue.text: Flipping admit it ref, England's holding on to legendary Egyptian

indicators.note: Flipping says the hidden letters are read backwards
holding on to says the words contain the answer within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An exasperated plea for a referee to concede England is clinging on.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'holding on to' as part of the definition; it is the indicator that the answer sits inside 'admit it ref, England's', so the definition is just 'legendary Egyptian'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefertiti was an ancient queen of Egypt, wife of Akhenaten, famous for her painted bust.

clue.text: Middle of Blackadder set ruined

indicators.note: Middle of says the central letters of the word are used

parts.note: to set something is to put it down

explanation.surface: The heart of the Blackadder set is in ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackadder is a British TV sitcom starring Rowan Atkinson; 'set' suggests a TV set, but it means put.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaput, from German, means broken and no longer working, so wrecked.

clue.text: Time phone company showed support

parts.note: EE is a British mobile phone network

explanation.surface: A phone company's timely show of backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tee is the peg that holds up a golf ball before it is driven.

clue.text: Nurses getting to grips with answer to crossword clue before journalist's aware

indicators.note: before says the first group comes ahead of the journalist
getting to grips with means holding, so the nurses enclose the next piece

parts.note: an EN is an enrolled nurse, so two of them make the plural
a light is a crossword answer, written into the grid
ED is the abbreviation for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Nurses grappling with a crossword answer before a journalist knows it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' is plural, so the enrolled-nurse abbreviation appears twice; in crossword jargon a light is a grid entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enlightened is to be well informed and knowledgeable, so aware of something.
